title: Align Azure helper command and install docs
body:
## Summary
Define one supported Azure helper command and document correct source-tree, Cabal, and Nix invocation paths.

## Evidence
- `README.md:66-81` tells installed users to run `azure-redis-connect`.
- The Nix default package actually installs the helper as `redis-connect` at `default.nix:53-75`.
- `docs/AZURE_EXAMPLES.md:18-21` says `cabal build` is sufficient, then `docs/AZURE_EXAMPLES.md:28-68` repeatedly invokes `python3 azure-redis-connect.py` as though the script were in the repository root; the tracked file is `scripts/azure-redis-connect.py`.
- `redis-client.cabal:130-153` installs only the Haskell `redis-client` executable, so the helper is not part of the Cabal install path described by the docs.

## User impact
Every documented helper entry point can fail depending on installation method: Nix users receive a differently named binary, source users are pointed at the wrong path, and Cabal users are not told how to expose either the helper or `redis-client` on `PATH`.

## Proposed direction
Choose a canonical installed name (preferably preserving a compatibility alias if renaming), make Nix packaging and docs agree, and explicitly document source checkout versus installed-package workflows.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] README command names match binaries produced by `nix profile install .#` and direct GitHub flake installation.
- [ ] Source-tree examples use the tracked `scripts/azure-redis-connect.py` path or an intentional root wrapper.
- [ ] Cabal instructions explain whether the Azure helper is supported and how `redis-client` becomes available on `PATH`.
- [ ] The old helper name remains as an alias or receives clear migration guidance.
- [ ] A smoke check verifies the documented helper command can at least print usage without Azure credentials.

title: Remove or implement inert client configuration fields
body:
## Summary
Ensure every public configuration field has observable behavior, eliminate duplicated policy knobs, and provide validated defaults/builders so users cannot construct configurations that are accepted but ignored.

## Evidence
- `hask-redis-mux/lib/cluster/Database/Redis/Standalone.hs:75-94` exposes `standaloneMultiplexerCount` and documents it as tunable.
- `hask-redis-mux/lib/cluster/Database/Redis/Standalone.hs:96-126` stores only one `Multiplexer` and never reads `standaloneMultiplexerCount`, so all configured values behave identically.
- `hask-redis-mux/lib/cluster/Database/Redis/Cluster/ConnectionPool.hs:36-42` exposes `connectionTimeout`, `maxRetries`, and `useTLS`; `connectionTimeout` is explicitly marked reserved and none of these fields participates in pool behavior.
- `hask-redis-mux/lib/cluster/Database/Redis/Cluster/Client.hs:139-146` separately exposes `clusterMaxRetries`, duplicating the inert `PoolConfig.maxRetries` concept.
- `hask-redis-mux/lib/cluster/Database/Redis/Cluster/Client.hs:229-245` hardcodes the cluster multiplexer count to `1` instead of making it part of the client configuration.
- `app/ClusterSetup.hs:68-84` populates all of these fields, giving CLI maintainers and users the impression they are effective.

## Impact
Configuration changes can appear successful while doing nothing, which makes performance tuning and reliability settings misleading. Duplicated retry/TLS policy also creates ambiguity about which layer owns behavior and makes compatibility evolution harder.

## Proposed direction
Define configuration by responsibility: transport/TLS belongs in the connector, pool capacity/timeouts belong in pool configuration, and retry/topology/multiplexer policy belongs in cluster/standalone client configuration. Wire supported fields through construction, remove or deprecate unsupported fields, add smart constructors/defaults, and validate positive/range-constrained values before allocating resources.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every exported configuration field is either implemented and tested or removed through an explicit compatibility/deprecation plan.
- [ ] `standaloneMultiplexerCount` changes the number of active multiplexers, or is removed/renamed to match actual semantics.
- [ ] Cluster multiplexer count is configurable without constructing a separate pool outside `ClusterClient`.
- [ ] Retry policy has one authoritative owner; pool and cluster settings do not duplicate it.
- [ ] Connection timeout is enforced with defined units and typed failure behavior, or is not exposed.
- [ ] TLS selection is represented by connector/type choice rather than an ignored Boolean.
- [ ] Default constructors/builders and invalid-value tests are added.
